resources.string: A shielded wallet for RAND. Balances and transfers are private by default; only your viewing key can open them.

This 64-character key is the wallet. There is no second copy: anyone who has it can spend, and if you lose it, nothing can recover your notes. Write it down or store it in a password manager before continuing.
I have saved my spend key somewhere safe
Paste a spend key (64 hex characters) or the contents of a wallet.key.json from the rand command-line wallet.
Unlock with your fingerprint, face or device PIN.
This device has no screen lock, so the wallet cannot be locked. Set one in Android settings to protect your spend key.
No activity yet. Ask the faucet for testnet RAND, or share your address.
Anyone can pay this address. It reveals nothing about what you hold.
Whoever pays you sees this fingerprint on their confirmation; if it does not match, it is not your address.
QR code of your payment link
This link is too long for a QR code; share or copy it instead.
Optional: ask for an amount, and add a note the payer’s wallet fills in for them.
Optional: ask for an amount the payer’s wallet fills in for them.
Enter the amount as a number, for example 1.25.
Scan a rand1 address or a randpay: link
Scanning needs the camera. Allow it in Android settings, or paste the link instead.
Encrypted with the payment: only the recipient, you and anyone either of you shows it to can read it.
Amount plus fee exceeds your balance.
No contacts yet. Add one from Contacts on the home screen.
That is not a rand1 address.
Enter an amount in RAND, up to 9 decimals.
Read the fingerprint back against the one the recipient sees on their Receive screen.
Proving the transfer takes a few minutes on a phone. Keep the app open; a notification shows progress if you switch away.

This proof needs about %1$s GB of memory and this phone has %2$s GB. Android will most likely stop the app before it finishes. Pair a prover in Settings › Prover, or send from the rand command-line wallet on a computer with the key file from Settings › Export.
A zero-knowledge proof authorises this transfer instead of a signature. About a few minutes on this device.
The transaction key opens exactly this payment on randscan.org and nothing else. Share it with the recipient or an auditor if they need to see it.
Copies the transaction key and opens the transaction on RandScan, where pasting the key reveals the amount and parties of this one payment.
No contacts yet. A contact\'s name can be typed in Send\'s To field instead of the address.
That is not a shielded address or a randpay: link.
Opens your whole history on RandScan — every note received and sent — but cannot spend. Paste it on the explorer\'s My history page.
The spend key moves your funds. Anyone who sees it can spend everything in this wallet. Continue?
Throws the note cache away and reads the whole tree again. Nothing is lost: notes are recovered by trial decryption.
This deletes the spend key from this device. Unless you saved it, every note it can open is lost forever. Remove?
Not marked as your own: it can read this wallet\'s whole history. It cannot spend.

Where this device cannot make a proof, pair a prover — rand-prover on a machine you run, or one somebody else runs, reachable from this phone over https. It receives this wallet\'s viewing key and a salt: it can read the wallet\'s whole history and cannot spend.
The randprover: link your prover shows. It carries a secret — paste it here and nowhere else. A prover must be reached over https (plain http only on this device).
Scan your prover\'s pairing QR code
This prover will be able to read this wallet\'s whole history — every payment received and sent, before and after today. It cannot spend. To keep your history private, run your own.

Or use the prover RandProtocol runs for everyone — %1$s, fingerprint %2$s. It charges nothing. It receives this wallet\'s viewing key, so it can read your whole history, past and future. It cannot spend.
%1$s prover · where this device cannot prove

The prover RandProtocol runs for everyone (%1$s), used until you choose another. It charges nothing. It receives this wallet\'s viewing key, so it can read your whole history, past and future. It cannot spend.
Using the %1$s prover. Proofs this device cannot make go to it. %2$s
No prover. Proofs are made on this device only; where it cannot make one, sending waits until you pair a prover or use the RandProtocol prover again.
Forgotten. The prover\'s pairing is gone from this wallet. Proofs this device cannot make go to the %1$s prover again.

This device does not have the memory for this proof, so the %1$s prover will make it. It receives your viewing key and a salt inside a sealed job — it can read this wallet\'s whole history and cannot spend; this phone authorises the spend itself and checks the proof before anything is sent.
The RandProtocol prover can read your history

This device cannot make the proof, so the prover RandProtocol runs for everyone makes it. It receives this wallet\'s viewing key, so it can read your whole history — every payment received and sent, past and future. It cannot spend. You are asked once; to keep your history to yourself, use your own prover instead.
Paired — this prover can read your history. Proofs this device cannot make go to %1$s. Its fingerprint is %2$s. %3$s
Not paired: paste the randprover: link your prover shows.
Paired. Proofs this device cannot make go to %1$s. Its fingerprint is %2$s — check that your prover shows the same.
Forgotten. Proofs are made on this device again. The prover\'s pairing is gone from this wallet.

This device does not have the memory for this proof, so your prover, %1$s, will make it. It receives your viewing key and a salt inside a sealed job — it can read this wallet\'s history and cannot spend; this phone authorises the spend itself and checks the proof before anything is sent.
Rand Wallet %1$s · core %2$s · chain build %3$s\nExperimental testnet software. Not audited; not for real value.
Keep Rand Wallet installed and the phone awake; this takes a few minutes.
